'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[2023 Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]]
***[[Israel]] calls on [[civilian]]s to [[emergency evacuation|evacuate]] [[Khan Yunis]] in the south of [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] and head to [[field hospital]]s, saying that [[Israeli Ground Forces|Israeli troops]] will be carrying out a [[military operation]] in the area. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-renews-call-gazans-flee-key-southern-city-2023-11-17/ (Reuters)]
**An [[Israeli Air Force|Israeli]] [[airstrike]] kills [[Ahmad Bahar (Palestinian politician)|Ahmad Bahar]], a senior leader in [[Hamas]] who served as the [[vice president]] of the [[Palestinian Legislative Council]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/palestinian-reports-hamas-official-ahmad-bahar-killed-in-israeli-strike-in-gaza/ (''Times of Israel'')]
**Ten [[fuel truck]]s enter Gaza from [[Egypt]] through the [[Rafah Border Crossing]], carrying 150,000 litres of [[diesel fuel]]. [https://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContent/58/1262/512407/War-on-Gaza/War-on-Gaza/Egypt-delivers-,-litres-of-diesel-to-Gaza-in-truck.aspx (''Al-Ahram'')]
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**[[Operation 1027]]
***The [[Tatmadaw|military]] recaptures the town of [[Pauktaw]], [[Rakhine State]], from the [[Arakan Army]] following heavy bombardment of the town. [https://myanmar-now.org/en/news/myanmar-junta-retakes-town-captured-by-aa-near-rakhine-capital/ (''Myanmar Now'')]
***A [[Myanmar Air Force]] [[warplane]] bombs a school in [[Chin State]], killing at least eight children. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-67448410 (BBC News)]
**[[Operation 1107]]
***[[Karenni people|Karenni]] rebels overrun [[Tatmadaw|military forces]] sheltering inside the district courthouse in [[Loikaw]], [[Kayah State]], subsequently setting the building on fire as fighting continues in the city. [https://www.irrawaddy.com/news/burma/thousands-in-loikaw-fear-myanmar-junta-bombs.html (''The Irrawaddy'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2022–2023 food crises]]
**[[Russia]] begins [[Russian grain exports|its shipments of free grain]] to [[Africa]] as part of [[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]]'s pledge to send 200,000 tonnes of grain to six [[African nations]]. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2023/11/17/russia-has-sent-first-free-grain-shipments-to-africa-a83141 (AFP via ''The Moscow Times'')]
*[[2023 United Auto Workers strike]]
**The [[United Auto Workers]] and [[General Motors]] ratify a contract to end the [[strike action|strike]] at General Motors plants across the [[United States]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/Business/uaw-members-ratify-deal-general-motors-1st-big/story?id=104941395 (ABC)]
*The [[Al Dhafra, Abu Dhabi|Al Dhafra]] [[Solar power in the United Arab Emirates|solar farm]], the largest [[photovoltaic power station|solar farm]] in the world, comes online in the [[United Arab Emirates]]. The [[solar farm]] is expected to power around 200,000 homes. [https://electrek.co/2023/11/17/worlds-largest-single-site-solar-farm/ (Electrek)]
*[[Sam Altman]] steps down as [[CEO]] of American [[artificial intelligence]] developer [[OpenAI]] following a vote from the company's [[board of directors]] demanding his resignation. In response, fellow co-founder [[Greg Brockman]] quits his role as president of OpenAI. [[Mira Murati]] takes over as interim CEO. [https://www.cnbc.com/2023/11/18/openais-structure-left-sam-altman-vulnerable-now-hes-out.html (CNBC)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[November 2023 Mindanao earthquake]]
** A magnitude 6.7 [[list of earthquakes in the Philippines|earthquake]] hits southern [[Mindanao]], [[Philippines]], killing at least seven people and leaving two others missing. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-11-17/magnitude-7-2-earthquake-shakes-southern-philippines (Bloomberg)]

'''International relations'''
*[[APEC United States 2023]]
**[[Japan–United States relations]]
***[[Japan]] and the [[United States]] finalize a [[United States dollar|$]]2.35 billion deal for the latter to export 400 [[Tomahawk (missile)|Tomahawk]] [[cruise missile]]s to the former. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20231117-us-approves-major-long-range-missile-deal-for-japan (AFP via France 24)]
**[[Philippines–United States relations]]
***The [[Philippines]] and the United States sign a deal for the latter to export [[nuclear technology]] and materials to the former. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/us-philippines-ink-landmark-deal-nuclear-cooperation-2023-11-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[Nagorno-Karabakh conflict]]
**The [[International Court of Justice]] orders [[Azerbaijan]] to facilitate the "safe, unimpeded, and expeditious" return of [[Forced displacement|displaced]] people to [[Nagorno-Karabakh]], following [[2023 Azerbaijani offensive in Nagorno-Karabakh|the country's offensive]], and to ensure [[freedom of movement]] for those wishing to leave or remain in the region. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20231117-azerbaijan-must-allow-safe-return-to-nagorno-karabakh-un-court (AFP via RFI)]
*[[Rohingya genocide case]]
**[[Canada]], [[Denmark]], [[France]], [[Germany]], the [[Netherlands]], and the [[United Kingdom]] formally join the [[genocide]] case at the [[International Court of Justice]] against [[Myanmar]], accusing Myanmar's [[military junta]] of committing genocide against the [[Rohingya people]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/11/17/five-european-nations-join-myanmar-genocide-case (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[ECOWAS Court]] rules that [[Senegal]] has not violated the [[Human rights in Senegal|rights]] of [[Opposition (politics)|opposition]] figure [[Ousmane Sonko]]. [https://guardian.ng/news/west-africa-court-says-senegal-did-not-violate-jailed-opponent-sonkos-rights/ (AFP via ''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2023 Liberian general election]]
**[[President of Liberia|Liberian President]] [[George Weah]] [[concession (politics)|concedes defeat]] to former [[Vice President of Liberia|Vice President]] [[Joseph Boakai]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/joseph-boakai-brink-liberian-presidency-vote-count-nears-completion-2023-11-17/ (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Twitter under Elon Musk]]
**[[Apple Inc.|Apple]], [[IBM]], [[Paramount Global]] and other [[multinational companies]] suspend their advertising on [[Twitter|X]] (formerly Twitter) in response to [[X Corp.|X]] chairman [[Elon Musk]]'s endorsement of the [[white genocide conspiracy theory]]. [https://www.axios.com/2023/11/17/apple-twitter-x-advertising-elon-musk-antisemitism-ads (Axios)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2023/11/17/technology/elon-musk-twitter-x-advertisers.html (''The New York Times'')]
**The [[European Commission]] suspends all paid advertising on X, citing the risk of "reputational damage" to the [[European Union|EU]], and "widespread concerns relating to the spread of [[disinformation]]" on the platform. [https://www.politico.eu/article/no-more-ads-elon-musk-x-twitter-european-commission-tell-staff/ (Politico)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023–24 Premier League]]
**[[Everton F.C.|Everton Football Club]] receives a 10-point deduction this season for breaching the [[Premier League]]'s profit and sustainability rules, having made losses of [[pound sterling|£]]124.5 million (around [[United States dollar|US$]]155 million) in the three years up to [[2021–22 Premier League|2021–22]], with the limit being £105 million ($131 million). It is the largest points deduction in the league's history. [https://apnews.com/article/everton-premier-league-points-deduction-finances-e5059e11494a8cb35c2d1e7dc5a62e8a (AP)]
